wedo_instance.description: Forensic comparison of Trigonometric and Logarithmic computational aids.

meta.philosophy: Computational efficiency is the substrate upon which the Enlightenment was built.

tasks.description: Analyze the geometric origins of Chord and Sine tables.
Trace the algorithmic pivot from Napier to Briggs.
Compare the integration of Log-Sines in celestial navigation.

analysis.trig_tables: Originating in the 2nd century BC with Hipparchus, these tables mapped spatial relationships (chords and sines) to solve astronomical measurements. They represent the 'Geometry of the Sphere.'
analysis.log_tables: Emerging in 1614 with John Napier, logs were an algorithmic intervention designed to reduce multiplication and division (O(n^2) effort) to addition and subtraction (O(n) effort).
analysis.the_convergence: The 17th-century 'Log-Sine' tables integrated both, allowing mariners to solve spherical triangles using simple arithmetic, effectively 'flattening' the computational difficulty of navigation.
